questions.solution:
Electronic configuration of divalent metal ion having atomic number 25 is

Total number of unpaired electrons=5

μ (Magnetic moment) =n(n+2)BM

where n= number of unpaired e

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : In octahedral complexes, when \(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}} \lt \mathrm{P}\) high spin complexes are formed. When \(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}} \gt \mathrm{P}\) low spin complexes are formed.
Statement (II) : In tetrahedral complexes because of \(\Delta_{\mathrm{t}} \lt \mathrm{P}\), low spin complexes are rarely formed.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In octahedral complex \((\mathrm{CN}=6)\)
If \(\Delta_0 \lt \) P.E., then high spin complexes are formed
If \(\Delta_0 \gt \) P.E., then low spin complexes are formed But in tetrahedral complex \((\mathrm{CN}=4)\)
\(\Delta_t \lt \) P.E., then mainly high spin complexes are formed and rarely low spin complexes are formed.

questions.q: The compound used in the treatment of lead poisoning is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
(1) Sodium calcium edetate, a salt of EDTA (Ethylene Diamine Tetra-acetic Acid), is used to bind metals in the chelation therapy, such as for treating mercury and lead poisoning.
(2) Cis-platin is used as an anti-cancer drug.

questions.q: The molecule/ion with square pyramidal shape is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
BrF5 is an interhalogen compound, meaning that the molecules of this compound contain two or more different halogen atoms but no atoms of the elements belonging to any other group.

The hybridisation of bromine pentafluoride forms an sp3d2 hybridisation, resulting in a square pyramidal molecular structure. The hybrid molecule has five sigma bonds due to the covalent electron sharing.

questions.solution:

questions.q: Complete removal of both the axial ligands (along the <math><mi mathvariant="normal">z</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> ) from an octahedral complex leads to which of the following splitting patterns? (relative orbital energies not on scale).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
When crystal field splitting energy is small, the pairing energy exceeds the splitting energy, and the electrons will fill the d orbitals as if they were degenerate; this is classified as high spin.

We find that the square planar complexes have the greatest crystal field splitting energy compared to all the other complexes. This means that most square planar complexes are low spin, strong field ligands.

questions.q: The observed magnetic moment of the complex <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>[</mo><mi>Mn</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>NCS</mi><msub><mo>)</mo><mn>6</mn></msub><mo>)</mo><msup><mo>]</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>06</mn><mo> </mo><mi>BM</mi></math>. The numerical value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The complex [Mn(NCS)6)]x- has a magnetic moment of 6.06 BM. This indicates that the complex has unpaired electrons, which contribute to its magnetic moment.

Number of unpaired electrons =5(Mn2+ : 3d5).
So Mn must be in +2 oxidation state Mn2+.

⇒ 2 + (–6) = –x ⇒ –4 = –x ⇒ x = 4
The numerical value of x is 4, so the complex is [Mn(NCS)6)]4-.
